summary: A 1934 CCC-built enclosed windmill-style tower on Tahoe NF, staffed every summer until 1975, now a popular Forest Service rental cab.

facts.design: C-3, 14'x14' wooden cab with catwalk on an enclosed 17-foot tower, enclosed windmill-style; living quarters on first landing

access.note: Restored and in the Forest Service rental program via Sierraville Ranger District; summer drive-up, winter access by snowshoe, ski, or snowmobile.

visit.trail_note: Drive to base in summer; winter requires snowshoes, skis or snowmobile. Only the top observation cab is rented.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as an enclosed windmill-style lookout.
Actively used for fire detection every summer until 1975.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 21, 2004 (per brief/NHLR record).
A renter reported being confronted and having their vehicle rammed by trespassers after midnight; incident reported to the sheriff.

evidence.supports: Built 1934 by CCC; C-3 cab design with catwalk on enclosed tower; living quarters on first landing.
evidence.quote: Built in 1934 by the CCC, it is a C-3 14'x14' wooden cab with catwalk on an enclosed 17' tower. Living quarters are on the first landing.

evidence.supports: Occasionally staffed during high lightning/fire danger per ranger station.
evidence.quote: May be staffed durring time of high lighting activity and high fire danger. This is perthe ranger station.

On July 16th, 2005, at about 40 minutes after midnight, three people, two men and a woman, came up to the tower to roust us out and to have fun... The driver yelled at me and then got into his mountain style vehicle and rammed my SUV.

evidence.supports: One of three remaining enclosed windmill-style lookouts in CA; staffed every summer until 1975.
evidence.quote: Calpine is a forest fire lookout tower that was constructed in 1934 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, and is one of three remaining examples of the enclosed windmill-style lookout in California. The lookout was actively used every summer until 1975.

evidence.supports: Rental details: only top cab rented, no electricity/water, elevation and distance from Truckee, seasonal access modes.
evidence.quote: Calpine sits at an elevation of 5,980 feet in the Sierra Nevada Mountains of the Tahoe National Forest, approximately 40 miles from Truckee, California. During the summer, renters can drive directly to the base of the tower. In winter, the road is often closed due to snow and ice so access is by snowshoes, skis or snowmobile.

notes_for_editor: Elevation differs slightly between the brief (1778.8 m / 5,836 ft) and Recreation.gov (5,980 ft) — not flagged as a correction since it's a minor discrepancy in secondary description text, but worth a glance if precision matters. Did not independently re-verify 2004 NHLR registration date beyond the brief. Verification pass 2026-10-04: removed the story's claim that the enclosed windmill-style design was 'common to CCC-era towers in California' -- neither source supports that; Recreation.gov instead says only three examples of this style survive, which argues the opposite of 'common.'
